verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same three rescalings, with two encoding choices. (i) The exponents match term by term: `axisExponent D = ![1/2, D, 1]` gives r/Q^{1/2}, z/Q^{D}, τ/Q, and `normalizedSlow_coordinates` prints the triple in that exact form. (ii) Lean's chart takes the remaining time τ as its third input coordinate instead of t, so the paper's `(1-t)/Q` is split into the substitution τ = 1-t (`timeShift p = (1 - p.1, p.2)`, and `physicalChart_time : (physicalChart h n p).1 = (1 - p.1)/Q n` for the Cartesian form of the same chart) followed by the division by Q. Recovery: slowCoordinates D n (r, z, 1-t) = C_ℓ(r,z,t) by unfolding axisExponent. (iii) `B_{ℓ,a} = supp χ_{ℓ,a}` has no named Lean constant; χ_{ℓ,a} is `SquaredPartition.slowMask n k` and B_{ℓ,a} is its `tsupport`, which `slowMask_tsupport_subset` places inside the one-mesh box around the grid point, as the paper's preceding sentence requires.
